column1: # The package set, and the single source of truth for it.
# BuildNugets.sh packs in this order, the release and PR workflows generate their package tables
# from it, and run-simulator-tests.sh clears the local NuGet cache for every id listed here.
# Adding a package means adding a row here and a project under src/ - nothing else has a second
# copy of the list to fall out of step with.
# package-id
SFMCSDK.Net.iOS
# NOT BOUND, and why.
#   MarketingCloudSDK        The MobilePush umbrella framework. Bound by the sibling repository,
#   AppGroupSDK              MarketingCloudSDK.Net.iOS (which also carries AppGroupSDK, the
#                            internal framework MobilePush requires), depending on this
#                            package for the core - mirroring the native package manifests.
#   PushFeatureSDK           The modular feature frameworks of the Unified SDK generation
#   IAMFeatureSDK            (push-feature-sdk-ios, iam-feature-sdk-ios, mam-core-sdk-ios).
#   MAMCoreSDK               Salesforce's integration docs route apps through the umbrella
#                            MarketingCloudSDK, which is what the sibling repository binds;
#                            these become packages of their own once a consumer needs one
#                            directly.
#   InboxFeatureSDK          The Inbox feature module (inbox-feature-sdk-ios), first published as
#                            1.0.0 alongside SFMCSDK 5.0.0. A separate framework that nothing
#                            here or in MobilePush 12's package manifest depends on, and not
#                            bound yet. This package carries the half the core shares with it:
#                            the Inbox models and events, and SFMCSdkConfigBuilder.SetInboxFeature,
#                            which is of no use from .NET until the module that supplies its
#                            configuration is bound too. It becomes a package of its own once a
#                            consumer needs Inbox.
